sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领导人，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、扎伊兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com网站直播部分采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费新闻阅读权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天是。

sentences.en: Last week, a long-awaited report showed that the worst consequences of global warming will occur even sooner than we thought.
sentences.zh: 上周，一份期待已久的报告显示，全球变暖带来的最严重后果将比我们预想的更早发生。

sentences.en: The story behind that report.
sentences.zh: 这份报告背后的故事。

sentences.en: It's Friday, October 19th.
sentences.zh: 今天是10月19日，星期五。

sentences.en: Mr. Secretary General, Monsieur le Président de la France, Your Excellencies.
sentences.zh: 秘书长先生，法国总统先生，各位阁下。

sentences.en: So back in 2015, when world leaders got together in Paris and forged the Paris Climate Agreement.
sentences.zh: 回到2015年，当时世界各国领导人在巴黎齐聚一堂，达成了《巴黎气候协定》。

sentences.en: It's an enormous privilege to be here on Earth Day to join in signing this historic agreement.
sentences.zh: 能在地球日签署这项历史性协议，我深感荣幸。

sentences.en: What it says is every country on Earth, every government would pass policies and take actions to lower emissions to stop climate change.
sentences.zh: 协议规定，地球上的每个国家、每个政府都将通过政策并采取行动，减少排放以阻止气候变化。

sentences.en: And there was a very specific target.
sentences.zh: 而且有一个非常具体的目标。

sentences.en: A mean temperature well below two degrees.
sentences.zh: 将平均气温控制在远低于两摄氏度的水平。

sentences.en: Two centigrade or even lower than that.
sentences.zh: 两摄氏度，甚至更低。

sentences.en: If we get to two degrees Celsius, Bangkok could be underwater.
sentences.zh: 如果我们达到两摄氏度，曼谷可能会被淹没在水下。

sentences.en: Two degrees Celsius or 3.6 degrees Fahrenheit over pre-industrial levels.
sentences.zh: 比工业化前水平高出两摄氏度或3.6华氏度。

sentences.en: Coral Davenport covers energy and the environment for the Times.
sentences.zh: 科拉尔·达文波特为《纽约时报》报道能源和环境新闻。

sentences.en: So for a couple of decades, that has been the point at which scientists really understood that the planet would tip into damages that would be severe and irreversible.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，科学家们一直认为，这就是地球将陷入严重且不可逆转的损害的临界点。

sentences.en: If nothing is done to curb emissions over the next couple of years, there will be a two-degree
sentences.zh: 如果未来几年不采取措施遏制排放，下个世纪的气温将升高两度，

sentences.en: change in the temperature of the next century, which is enough for some cataclysmic event.
sentences.zh: 这足以引发某些灾难性事件。

sentences.en: Severe droughts, severe food losses.
sentences.zh: 严重的干旱，严重的粮食减产。

sentences.en: In the two-degree world, people are poorer and have less food.
sentences.zh: 在两度升温的世界里，人们更贫穷，食物更匮乏。

sentences.en: Extremely devastating and damaging storMs.
sentences.zh: 极具破坏性和毁灭性的风暴。

sentences.en: The higher frequency of severe weather conditions taking place throughout the world.
sentences.zh: 全球范围内极端天气状况的频率增加。

sentences.en: Melting of the polar ice sheets, major sea level rise, loss of coastal habitat.
sentences.zh: 极地冰盖融化、海平面大幅上升、沿海栖息地丧失。

sentences.en: And all the coral in our seas has gone.
sentences.zh: 而且我们海洋中所有的珊瑚都消失了。

sentences.en: And keep in mind, we're already halfway there.
sentences.zh: 请记住，我们已经走了一半的路程。

sentences.en: The planet's already warmed about one degree Celsius since the 1850s.
sentences.zh: 自1850年代以来，地球已经变暖了约一摄氏度。

sentences.en: It sounds like a really small margin, but it could make the difference between billions of people facing droughts in Africa or not.
sentences.zh: 这听起来是一个很小的幅度，但它可能决定了非洲是否有数十亿人面临干旱。

sentences.en: It's really just one more degree of warming that brings us those outcomes.
sentences.zh: 仅仅再升高一度，就会带来这些后果。

sentences.en: So we're basically halfway towards climate Armageddon.
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上已经走了一半通往气候末日的路。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Coral, when do we expect to reach that pretty terrifying tipping point of a two-degree increase?
sentences.zh: 科拉尔，我们预计什么时候会达到两度升温这个相当可怕的临界点？

sentences.en: Well, it's been understood for the past couple of decades that that two degrees of warming will hit sometime in the second half of the 21st century.
sentences.zh: 嗯，过去几十年来人们一直认为，两度升温将在21世纪下半叶的某个时候到来。

sentences.en: So it's not today, it's not tomorrow, but it's within sight.
sentences.zh: 所以不是今天，也不是明天，但已经指日可待了。

sentences.en: So basically any time after 2050.
sentences.zh: 基本上就是2050年之后的任何时候。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But what's interesting is that in Paris, as the accord was being written and put together,
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，在巴黎，当协议正在起草和制定时，

sentences.en: a lot of the smaller and more vulnerable countries in the world, particularly small island nations
sentences.zh: 世界上许多较小且更脆弱的国家，特别是小岛屿国家，

sentences.en: that are experiencing some of the impacts of climate change, particularly rising sea
sentences.zh: 它们正在经历气候变化的一些影响，特别是海平面上升、

sentences.en: levels, loss of their homes, they're experiencing their freshwater supplies soaked by saltwater,
sentences.zh: 家园丧失，它们的淡水供应被海水浸泡，

sentences.en: countries that are starting to live the impact of climate change now kind of raised their hand
sentences.zh: 这些现在开始感受到气候变化影响的国家在巴黎举手说，

sentences.en: in Paris and said, hey, we know the goal of this is to avoid that two degrees of warming, but can we also take a look at what 1.5 degrees of warming looks like?
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们知道这个目标是为了避免两度升温，但我们能不能也看看1.5度升温是什么样子？

sentences.en: We wonder if bad things might happen halfway to that two-degree point.
sentences.zh: 我们想知道在达到两度升温的一半时，是否会发生糟糕的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe half a degree matters more than we think.
sentences.zh: 也许半度的影响比我们想象的要大。

sentences.en: Maybe not.
sentences.zh: 也许不是。

sentences.en: Let's find out.
sentences.zh: 让我们一探究竟。

sentences.en: And so the rest of the world, the other countries said, okay, we're not going to change the target.
sentences.zh: 于是世界其他国家说，好吧，我们不会改变目标。

sentences.en: We're settled around two degrees here, but let's assign the world's best climate scientists to tell us what 1.5 degrees earlier warming looks like.
sentences.zh: 我们已经确定了两度这个目标，但让我们指派世界上最顶尖的气候科学家来告诉我们1.5度升温是什么样子。

sentences.en: Let's make the vulnerable countries happy and just kind of figure that out.
sentences.zh: 让脆弱的国家满意，我们弄清楚这一点就行了。

sentences.en: So what happens with this study?
sentences.zh: 那么这项研究的结果如何？

sentences.en: So the scientists got this assignment at the end of 2015.
sentences.zh: 科学家们在2015年底接到了这个任务。

sentences.en: The group chosen to work on this was 91 scientists from 42 countries.
sentences.zh: 被选中参与这项工作的团队由来自42个国家的91名科学家组成。

sentences.en: They went to work together.
sentences.zh: 他们开始共同工作。

sentences.en: They reviewed about 6,000 published studies.
sentences.zh: 他们审查了大约6000项已发表的研究。

sentences.en: They responded to about 42,000 comments from governments and other scientists.
sentences.zh: 他们回复了来自政府和其他科学家的约42000条意见。

sentences.en: All the scientists do this voluntarily.
sentences.zh: 所有的科学家都是自愿参与的。

sentences.en: They don't get paid.
sentences.zh: 他们没有报酬。

sentences.en: So they worked for a year and a half on it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们为此工作了一年半。

sentences.en: Good morning, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家早上好。

sentences.en: Welcome to this press conference of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change to present the special report on global warming of 1.5 degrees.
sentences.zh: 欢迎参加政府间气候变化专门委员会的新闻发布会，发布关于全球变暖1.5度的特别报告。

sentences.en: A couple of weeks ago, I went to the city of Incheon in South Korea, where all of the 91 authors of this report were gathered.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我去了韩国仁川市，报告的所有91位作者都聚集在那里。

sentences.en: I'm going to hand over now to the chair of the IPCC, Dr. Lee, who will give you an introduction to the report.
sentences.zh: 现在我将把话筒交给IPCC主席李博士，他将为您介绍这份报告。

sentences.en: And then the co-chairs will give you some information about the report and go through the highlights.
sentences.zh: 然后联合主席将为您提供有关报告的一些信息，并介绍重点内容。

sentences.en: And then we'll be very happy.
sentences.zh: 届时我们将非常乐意。

sentences.en: And in South Korea, what did they tell you about the report?
sentences.zh: 在韩国，他们向你介绍了关于报告的什么内容？

sentences.en: What did they find?
sentences.zh: 他们发现了什么？

sentences.en: It first of all tells us 1.5 degrees of warming looks a lot more like 2 degrees of warming than we thought.
sentences.zh: 首先，它告诉我们，1.5度升温看起来比我们想象的更接近2度升温。

sentences.en: Limiting warming to 1.5 degrees C implies changes on an unprecedented scale.
sentences.zh: 将升温限制在1.5摄氏度意味着前所未有的规模变革。

sentences.en: That we're going to experience a lot of those same outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我们将经历许多同样的后果。

sentences.en: We're going to experience major loss of sea ice, major loss of coral reefs.
sentences.zh: 我们将经历海冰的大量流失，珊瑚礁的大量死亡。

sentences.en: The impacts of climate change in the oceans are increasing risks to fisheries and livelihoods that depend on them.
sentences.zh: 气候变化对海洋的影响正在增加渔业和依赖渔业的生计的风险。

sentences.en: Major droughts and subsequent crop loss.
sentences.zh: 严重的干旱和随之而来的农作物减产。

sentences.en: Thus, a lot of food shortages.
sentences.zh: 因此，会出现大量的粮食短缺。

sentences.en: A lot of coastal inundation as well.
sentences.zh: 还有大量的沿海淹没。

sentences.en: Probably tens of millions of people losing their homes, losing their livelihoods.
sentences.zh: 可能有数千万人失去家园，失去生计。

sentences.en: All that stuff happens at a lower temperature.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情在较低的温度下就会发生。

sentences.en: The damaging impacts come with less warming than we thought.
sentences.zh: 破坏性的影响在比我们预想更低的升温幅度下就会出现。

sentences.en: And that also means that they come sooner in time.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着它们在时间上会更早到来。

sentences.en: Global temperature is likely to reach 1.5 degrees C between 2030 to 2052.
sentences.zh: 全球气温很可能在2030年至2052年间达到1.5摄氏度。

sentences.en: So within most of our lifetimes.
sentences.zh: 所以就在我们大多数人的有生之年。

sentences.en: It's literally like around the corner.
sentences.zh: 简直就在眼前。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: From everything you've said, Coral, the world has been very much planning around staving off a 2 degree warming.
sentences.zh: 根据你所说的一切，科拉尔，世界一直在很大程度上计划着避免两度升温。

sentences.en: And now we have this new math that says that 1.5 degrees warming is almost as bad and something that must be avoided.
sentences.zh: 现在我们有了这个新的计算结果，显示1.5度升温几乎同样糟糕，是必须避免的。

sentences.en: Which makes me wonder how much the world is prepared to deal with that new reality.
sentences.zh: 这让我怀疑世界在多大程度上准备好应对这一新现实。

sentences.en: So since this was commissioned by world leaders for world leaders, the scientists did something else in this report that I pretty much don't ever see,
sentences.zh: 由于这份报告是世界领导人为世界领导人委托编写的，科学家们在报告中做了另一件我几乎从未见过的事情，

sentences.en: which is they laid out essentially some policy prescriptions for how to do it.
sentences.zh: 那就是他们基本上列出了一些政策处方，说明该如何做到这一点。

sentences.en: Rapid breakthroughs in technology, changes to the way we do farming, changes to the way we drive.
sentences.zh: 技术的快速突破，农业方式的改变，驾驶方式的改变。

sentences.en: But at the center, there is one economic policy that could sort of be the driver of all of this change.
sentences.zh: 但在核心，有一项经济政策可以成为所有这些变革的驱动力。

sentences.en: And that is a price or a tax on carbon dioxide pollution.
sentences.zh: 那就是对二氧化碳污染定价或征税。

sentences.en: And if you look at the report and you look at the section that describes this at several points about the importance and the powerful effectiveness of pricing or taxing carbon dioxide pollution,
sentences.zh: 如果你查看报告，查看描述这一点的部分，在多处提到了对二氧化碳污染定价或征税的重要性和强大有效性，

sentences.en: you see again and again and again, one name is mentioned, a Yale economist named William Nordhaus.
sentences.zh: 你会一次又一次地看到一个名字被提及，一位名叫威廉·诺德豪斯的耶鲁大学经济学家。

sentences.en: After the break, a conversation with William Nordhaus.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我们将与威廉·诺德豪斯进行对话。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费探索《纽约时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 一个月的时间让你越过付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果您还没有订阅《纽约时报》，请立即下载《纽约时报》应用程序，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has today decided to award the Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in memory of Alfred Nobel.
sentences.zh: 瑞典皇家科学院今天决定将瑞典国家银行纪念阿尔弗雷德·诺贝尔经济学奖授予。

sentences.en: So on the same day that this new climate report came out, this economist, William Nordhaus, whose idea is cited throughout the report as the central solution to climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以，就在这份新的气候报告发布的那一天，这位经济学家威廉·诺德豪斯，他的观点在报告中被引用为应对气候变化的核心解决方案。

sentences.en: With one half to William D.
sentences.zh: 其中一半授予威廉·D·

sentences.en: Nordhaus.
sentences.zh: 诺德豪斯。

sentences.en: Also won the Nobel Prize in economics.
sentences.zh: 也获得了诺贝尔经济学奖。

sentences.en: For integrating climate change into long-run macroeconomic analysis.
sentences.zh: 以表彰他将气候变化整合到长期宏观经济分析中。

sentences.en: Is that a coincidence?
sentences.zh: 这是一个巧合吗？

sentences.en: I'm going to go with no.
sentences.zh: 我的回答是不会。

sentences.en: And the Nobel Committee was very clear that they were awarding this prize to William Nordhaus specifically for coming up with the idea of a carbon tax to solve global warming.
sentences.zh: 诺贝尔委员会非常明确地表示，他们将该奖项授予威廉·诺德豪斯，正是因为他提出了碳税这一解决全球变暖的想法。

sentences.en: Nordhaus asks, how should economists appropriately address climate change?
sentences.zh: 诺德豪斯问道，经济学家应该如何恰当地应对气候变化？

sentences.en: I think it's highly unlikely that that's a coincidence.
sentences.zh: 我认为这极不可能是巧合。

sentences.en: So that was last Monday.
sentences.zh: 那是上周一的事。

sentences.en: Two days later, I flew back home from Korea.
sentences.zh: 两天后，我从韩国飞回家。

sentences.en: And the next day, I went to visit William Nordhaus at Yale.
sentences.zh: 第二天，我去耶鲁大学拜访了威廉·诺德豪斯。

sentences.en: And the first thing I did was sit in on his Econ 122 class.
sentences.zh: 我做的第一件事就是旁听了他的经济学122课程。

sentences.en: I should say that he asked for the class to be off the record, so I should probably keep to myself what I learned.
sentences.zh: 我应该说，他要求这堂课不公开，所以我可能应该对自己学到的东西保密。

sentences.en: You've got a geeky class today.
sentences.zh: 你今天上了一堂极客课。

sentences.en: It was a good class.
sentences.zh: 这是一堂好课。

sentences.en: I enjoyed it.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢。

sentences.en: It was a geeky class.
sentences.zh: 这是一堂极客课。

sentences.en: That's appropriate.
sentences.zh: 这很贴切。

sentences.en: Okay, let's go.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们开始吧。

sentences.en: And what exactly is this idea of carbon pricing?
sentences.zh: 那么碳定价这个概念到底是什么？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Let me just talk about the idea a minute.
sentences.zh: 让我谈谈这个想法。

sentences.en: So this idea, which sort of gradually emerged in my mind, it wasn't something that just immediately the light bulb went off.
sentences.zh: 所以这个想法，在我脑海中逐渐形成，并不是那种灵光一现的东西。

sentences.en: So it's kind of a basic idea that a lot of governments use to tax things that you want less of.
sentences.zh: 这是一种很多政府用来对你想要减少的东西征税的基本理念。

sentences.en: Pollution taxes are not uncommon.
sentences.zh: 污染税并不罕见。

sentences.en: That's a pretty standard way to sort of disincentivize pollution.
sentences.zh: 这是一种抑制污染的相当标准的方法。

sentences.en: But no one had ever sort of thought of applying that idea to carbon dioxide before.
sentences.zh: 但以前没有人想到过将这个想法应用于二氧化碳。

sentences.en: Environmentalists hadn't.
sentences.zh: 环保主义者没有。

sentences.en: Scientists hadn't.
sentences.zh: 科学家没有。

sentences.en: And economists weren't really thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 经济学家也没有真正考虑过这一点。

sentences.en: So he really brought these disciplines together.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实把这些学科结合在了一起。

sentences.en: If you think of the people who are concerned about the environment, people concerned about climate change, I have many friends who do environmental science.
sentences.zh: 如果你想到那些关心环境的人，关心气候变化的人，我有很多从事环境科学的朋友。

sentences.en: And so this was not on their radar screen for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 所以这在很长一段时间内都没有引起他们的注意。

sentences.en: Not on their radar.
sentences.zh: 不在他们的考虑范围内。

sentences.en: Not on their radar screen.
sentences.zh: 不在他们的雷达监测范围内。

sentences.en: His idea, his sort of breakthrough idea was, how can we apply economics to the environmental damage that we know is caused by carbon dioxide?
sentences.zh: 他的想法，或者说他那种突破性的想法是：我们该如何将经济学应用到我们已知由二氧化碳造成的环境破坏上？

sentences.en: And so William Nordhaus created this economic model that looked at the science of climate change and how much damage is caused by heat trapping emissions and how you can extract from that the amount of damage caused by a single ton of carbon.
sentences.zh: 于是威廉·诺德豪斯（William Nordhaus）创建了这个经济模型，它审视了气候变化的科学原理，分析了温室气体排放造成了多少损害，以及如何从中推算出每一吨碳所造成的损害量。

sentences.en: I think if this does anything, I hope it points out the importance of pricing.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果这有什么作用的话，我希望它能指出定价的重要性。

sentences.en: Because unlike a lot of pollution, you know, carbon dioxide is invisible.
sentences.zh: 因为与许多污染不同，你知道，二氧化碳是看不见的。

sentences.en: You can't see it.
sentences.zh: 你看不见它。

sentences.en: You can't touch it.
sentences.zh: 你摸不着它。

sentences.en: It goes up in the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 它上升到了大气层中。

sentences.en: It's a very abstract thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常抽象的东西。

sentences.en: But when you're able to say, OK, one ton of carbon causes $50 of damage.
sentences.zh: 但当你能说，好吧，一吨碳造成了50美元的损失。

sentences.en: Two tons of carbon cause $100 of damage.
sentences.zh: 两吨碳造成了100美元的损失。

sentences.en: And that damage is quantified in things like rising sea levels that would, say, damage your home and, you know, raise your insurance costs and lower your property values.
sentences.zh: 而这种损害被量化为诸如海平面上升之类的事情，比如会损害你的房屋，你知道，提高你的保险成本并降低你的房产价值。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Well, that cost has been inflicted by a certain amount of carbon dioxide.
sentences.zh: 那么，这个成本就是由一定量的二氧化碳造成的。

sentences.en: It's a complicated model.
sentences.zh: 这是一个复杂的模型。

sentences.en: He called it the social cost of carbon.
sentences.zh: 他称之为碳的社会成本。

sentences.en: So it sounds like his breakthrough is figuring out a way of putting a literal price tag.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来他的突破在于找到了一种方法，可以给它贴上一个实实在在的价格标签。

sentences.en: Literal price tag.
sentences.zh: 实实在在的价格标签。

sentences.en: On the damage caused by climate change and then applying that as a kind of price on the producer.
sentences.zh: 给气候变化造成的损害贴上标签，然后将其作为一种生产者需要承担的价格。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Pricing carbon, putting a price on this, ending the subsidy that firms have to put their carbon dioxide in the atmosphere is the first step we need to take.
sentences.zh: 对碳进行定价，给它设定一个价格，结束企业向大气中排放二氧化碳所享有的补贴，这是我们需要采取的第一步。

sentences.en: That was a true breakthrough.
sentences.zh: 那是一个真正的突破。

sentences.en: Once he came up with the social cost of carbon, then you can apply that to policy.
sentences.zh: 一旦他提出了碳的社会成本，你就可以将其应用于政策。

sentences.en: You can take that over to the realm of governments dealing with carbon pollution and you can, in a perfect world, use it as a tax.
sentences.zh: 你可以将其带入政府处理碳污染的领域，在理想的情况下，你可以将其用作税收。

sentences.en: So if we go back to the basic idea of carbon pricing,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们回到碳定价的基本理念，

sentences.en: which is that you want to raise the prices of carbon-intensive products so consumers buy less of them and producers find less carbon-intensive ways of producing them.
sentences.zh: 那就是你想要提高碳密集型产品的价格，这样消费者就会少买，而生产者也会寻找碳排放强度较低的生产方式。

sentences.en: And what the scientists who wrote this new report and what economists who have been studying this issue for years have said is this is pretty much the most powerful and effective way to stop greenhouse gas emissions.
sentences.zh: 而撰写这份新报告的科学家们以及多年来一直研究这个问题的经济学家们所说的是，这几乎是阻止温室气体排放最强大、最有效的方法。

sentences.en: If polluters have to pay the same amount that they're damaging the environment to pollute, you are going to create all kinds of market signals.
sentences.zh: 如果污染者必须为他们对环境造成的破坏支付同样的代价，你就会创造出各种各样的市场信号。

sentences.en: Consumers will consume less carbon-intensive electricity, but also producers will move from coal to natural gas and natural gas to, say, wind.
sentences.zh: 消费者会减少对碳密集型电力的消费，而生产者也会从煤炭转向天然气，再从天然气转向风能等能源。

sentences.en: So these are the obvious substitution effects.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是显而易见的替代效应。

sentences.en: Electric utilities are going to say, wow, wind and solar are suddenly looking a lot cheaper.
sentences.zh: 电力公司会说，哇，风能和太阳能突然看起来便宜多了。

sentences.en: So a firm like GE, which does all kinds of energy, would know that it should invest its money in, say, wind turbines rather than turbines for coal-fired plants.
sentences.zh: 因此，像通用电气（GE）这样涉足各种能源业务的公司，就会知道它应该把钱投资在风力涡轮机上，而不是燃煤电厂的涡轮机上。

sentences.en: That's where the future is.
sentences.zh: 那才是未来所在。

sentences.en: And that it's not because it's a socially responsible corporation.
sentences.zh: 而且这并不是因为它是一家具有社会责任感的公司。

sentences.en: It's because it's a profit-oriented corporation.
sentences.zh: 这是因为它是一家以利润为导向的公司。

sentences.en: And if it sees these prices, carbon prices, going in that direction, it will know where to put its innovation dollars.
sentences.zh: 如果它看到这些价格，即碳价格，正朝着那个方向发展，它就会知道该把创新资金投向哪里。

sentences.en: What economists will tell you is these market forces are so much more powerful, you know, than altruism or a sense of moral or social responsibility.
sentences.zh: 经济学家会告诉你，这些市场力量比利他主义或道德、社会责任感要强大得多。

sentences.en: When the market is speaking, when you as a consumer say, all right, because of that carbon tax, the price of gasoline is now going to be $6, $7, $8, $9 a gallon permanently.
sentences.zh: 当市场在说话时，当你作为消费者说，好吧，因为那个碳税，汽油价格现在将永久性地达到每加仑6美元、7美元、8美元、9美元。

sentences.en: Forget it.
sentences.zh: 算了吧。

sentences.en: I'm never going to buy a gas guzzler again.
sentences.zh: 我再也不会买油老虎了。

sentences.en: I don't want my electricity from coal-fired power.
sentences.zh: 我不想用燃煤发电的电。

sentences.en: However, that is so much more expensive.
sentences.zh: 然而，那太昂贵了。

sentences.en: And electric utilities, who are the ones who buy the electricity, are going to say, that's too expensive.
sentences.zh: 而购买电力的电力公司会说，那太贵了。

sentences.en: Let's invest hugely and heavily in cleaner power right now.
sentences.zh: 让我们现在就大量投资于更清洁的能源。

sentences.en: And so, you know, in a theoretical way, economists have looked at this and they've said, this is the way to send a market signal.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，从理论上讲，经济学家们审视了这一点，他们说，这就是发送市场信号的方法。

sentences.en: And, you know, if we see this implemented around the world, that is how you turn around the entire global economy.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果我们看到这一点在世界各地实施，那就是你扭转整个全球经济的方式。

sentences.en: And it was that idea that Nordhaus won the Nobel for and that the scientists who wrote this new climate report elevated and said, look, this is it.
sentences.zh: 正是因为这个想法，诺德豪斯获得了诺贝尔奖，也正是撰写这份新气候报告的科学家们所推崇的，他们说，看，就是这个。

sentences.en: This is the solution.
sentences.zh: 这就是解决方案。

sentences.en: This is what we've got to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们必须做的。

sentences.en: So basically, his plan is to create a market incentive to solve climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他的计划是创造一种市场激励机制来解决气候变化问题。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Stick a price on it and then the market does the reSt.
sentences.zh: 给它贴上价格，然后市场就会完成剩下的工作。

sentences.en: Well, I have the view that we need a global program.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的观点是我们需要一个全球性的计划。

sentences.en: But Nordhaus is pretty clear.
sentences.zh: 但诺德豪斯说得很清楚。

sentences.en: In order for this to work, the only way you're going to have a global program is to have cooperation of nations, not cooperation of all the other countries in the world and 50 U.S.
sentences.zh: 为了让这个计划奏效，你拥有全球计划的唯一途径是各国之间的合作，而不是所有其他国家与美国50个州之间的合作。

sentences.en: states.
sentences.zh: 大多数国家都必须这样做。

sentences.en: Most countries have to do this.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，美国目前没有联邦碳税。

sentences.en: And to be clear, there's no federal carbon tax right now in the United States.
sentences.zh: 没有，没有联邦碳税。

sentences.en: No, there's no federal carbon tax.
sentences.zh: 没有联邦碳价格。

sentences.en: There's no federal carbon price.
sentences.zh: 一些州尝试过不同形式的碳定价，最著名的是加利福尼亚州。

sentences.en: Some states have experimented with different forms of carbon pricing, most notably California.
sentences.zh: 那么世界上有任何地方在国家层面部署过吗？

sentences.en: And has it ever been deployed at a national level anywhere in the world?
sentences.zh: 有。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 我想人们可能没有意识到它在国外受到了多大的欢迎。

sentences.en: I think people may not be aware of how much it's been embraced abroad.
sentences.zh: 关于碳定价的想法，我发现真正有趣且讽刺的是，它在美国被认为在政治上是有毒的。

sentences.en: What I find to be really interesting and ironic about the idea of carbon pricing is that it's considered sort of politically toxic in the United States.
sentences.zh: 然而它正在世界各地被实施。

sentences.en: And yet it's being implemented all around the world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它在欧洲被广泛使用。

sentences.en: I mean, it's widely used in Europe.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚实施了碳定价系统。

sentences.en: Australia put in place a carbon pricing system.
sentences.zh: 模范计划是不列颠哥伦比亚省的那一个。

sentences.en: The model plan is the one in British Columbia.
sentences.zh: 加拿大正朝着明年实现全国碳价格的方向迈进。

sentences.en: Canada is moving forward to a national carbon price by next year.
sentences.zh: 它现在正在中国逐步引入。

sentences.en: It's now being gradually introduced in China.
sentences.zh: 所以世界上大多数主要经济体至少已经开始实施某种形式的碳定价，或者正在区域内实施，并计划在国家或联邦层面进行推广。

sentences.en: So most of the world's major economies are at least starting to implement some form of carbon pricing or implement it regionally with a plan to do it at the national or federal level.
sentences.zh: 在美国，它绝对是胎死腹中。

sentences.en: At the United States, it's absolutely DOA.
sentences.zh: 究竟是什么阻碍了美国尝试碳定价，如果我们的许多伙伴国家都在这样做的话？

sentences.en: What exactly keeps the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国政治。

sentences.en: from experimenting with carbon pricing if so many of our fellow nations are doing it?
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，这项特定的政策受到了一群思想家的愤怒抵制，如果我可以这样说的话。

sentences.en: U.S.
sentences.zh: 税收在政治上已经变得有毒了。

sentences.en: politics.
sentences.zh: 有一位强大的反税收游说者格罗弗·诺奎斯特（Grover Norquist），他让共和党国会议员签署承诺，保证他们永远不会投票支持增税。

sentences.en: And it just happens that this particular policy is one that has sort of faced the wrath of a whole group of thinkers, if I could say that.
sentences.zh: 这是你能想象到的最大、最具争议的增税措施。

sentences.en: Taxes have become politically toxic.
sentences.zh: 自由意志主义亿万富翁查尔斯·科赫（Charles Koch）和大卫·科赫（David Koch）对此一直持绝对坚定的反对态度。

sentences.en: There is a powerful anti-tax lobbyist, Grover Norquist, who has Republican members of Congress sign pledges that they will never vote to raise taxes.
sentences.zh: 他们是政治倡导运动的主要捐助者。

sentences.en: This is the biggest and most controversial tax increase that you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 你知道，提高能源成本、增加税收、做一些由联合国支持的全球性事情的想法。

sentences.en: The libertarian billionaires, Charles and David Koch, have been absolutely out front in rock-solid opposition to this.
sentences.zh: 就其政治而言，这正是目前美国政治中许多强大势力所反对的核心所在。

sentences.en: They're, you know, major contributors to political advocacy campaigns.
sentences.zh: 那么，对于美国国内这种看似极其强大的反对之墙，他怎么看？

sentences.en: You know, the idea of raising energy costs, raising taxes, doing some kind of global thing that's endorsed by the U.N.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你能说什么呢？

sentences.en: And in terms of the politics of this, this is sort of at the heart of kind of everything that is politically opposed by so many of these powerful forces in U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，关于特朗普、特朗普的环境政策或麦康奈尔（McConnell），你能说什么？

sentences.en: politics right now.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们两者都没有连贯的环境政策。

sentences.en: And what does he say about what feels like an incredibly formidable wall of opposition inside the United States to this plan?
sentences.zh: 他们只对政治层面的事情感兴趣。

sentences.en: Well, it's what can you say?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他看得比较长远。

sentences.en: I mean, what can you say about Trump, Trump's environmental policies or McConnell?
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，事情会发生变化。

sentences.en: I mean, there's no coherent environmental policy there for either of those.
sentences.zh: 但他绝对承认，就在此刻，由于当前的政治力量，在美国通过碳税是不可能的。

sentences.en: They're only interested in the political side of things.
sentences.zh: 我们只需要继续向人们解释它。

sentences.en: Well, he takes the long view.
sentences.zh: 当特朗普政府及其灾难性的政策消失后，我们就会有合适的人选。

sentences.en: Things change over the long run.
sentences.zh: 我认为无论是共和党还是民主党，他们都会想要拥抱全世界都认为重要、许多美国人也认为重要的事情。

sentences.en: But he absolutely acknowledges that right this minute, because of the current sort of set of political forces, it would not be possible to pass a carbon tax in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 鉴于此，即使诺德豪斯也承认这在美国政治上是胎死腹中的，为什么科学家们仍然认为碳定价系统，

sentences.en: And we just have to continue explaining it to people.
sentences.zh: 即碳税，是抵御全球变暖最坏影响的最有效方法？

sentences.en: And when the Trump administration and its disastrous policies are gone, then we'll have someone there.
sentences.zh: 如果它不会在像美国这样的地方实施，为什么他们还要把它作为防止我们达到1.5度或2度升温计划的核心？

sentences.en: I think whether Republican or Democratic, they will want to embrace something the entire world feels is important and many Americans feel important.
sentences.zh: 嗯，科学家们也生活在政治现实中。

sentences.en: Given that, the fact that even Nordhaus concedes that this is politically kind of dead on arrival in the U.S., why do the scientists believe that a carbon pricing system,
sentences.zh: 这份报告的一个重要结论是，他们说，你知道，1.5度升温是什么样子。

sentences.en: a carbon tax, is the most effective way to stave off the worst effects of global warming?
sentences.zh: 2度升温是什么样子。

sentences.en: Why are they making that the linchpin of their plan to keep us from getting to 1.5 degree warming or keep us from getting to 2 degree warming if it's not going to be implemented in places like the United States?
sentences.zh: 如何避免这些情况。

sentences.en: Well, the scientists live in political reality as well.
sentences.zh: 他们给出了另一个情景，他们称之为“超调”情景。

sentences.en: And one of the big takeaways from this report is that they said, you know, here's what 1.5 degrees of warming looks like.
sentences.zh: 他们说，如果我们继续以现在的速度前进，这就是会发生的情况，我们达到了1.5度，

sentences.en: Here's what 2 degrees of warming looks like.
sentences.zh: 我们没有通过到处实施碳定价来迅速扭转全球经济。

sentences.en: Here's how to avoid those.
sentences.zh: 然后可能在2040年代的某个时候，当那些损害已经发生时，

sentences.en: And they gave another scenario, which they called the overshoot scenario.
sentences.zh: 那可能是全球政府和经济体真正采取行动并进行碳定价的时候。

sentences.en: They said, this is what it looks like if we keep going at the rate we're going, we hit that 1.5 degrees,
sentences.zh: 然后我们看到排放量下降，我们看到能够减少大气中碳排放的技术得到发展。

sentences.en: we don't turn around the global economy on a dime by carbon pricing everywhere.
sentences.zh: 所以我们先超调，然后再降下来。

sentences.en: And then maybe sometime in the 2040s when those damages have already hit,
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像他们预料到世界，也许是以美国为首，将无法采取行动，无法按照他们的建议采用碳定价，

sentences.en: that may be the time that global governments and economies actually get their act together and go ahead and do some carbon pricing.
sentences.zh: 而这种失败的后果，即对像美国和世界其他国家造成的痛苦，将促使美国采取碳定价。

sentences.en: And we see emissions go down and we see technology develop that could reduce carbon emissions from the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 这就是你要说的吗？

sentences.en: And so we overshoot and then we come back down.
sentences.zh: 这就是科学家们设想并写入报告的一个具体情景。

sentences.en: It's almost like they anticipate that the world, perhaps led by the United States, will fail to act, will fail to adopt carbon pricing as they recommend,
sentences.zh: 所以他们研究了如果排放量上升，我们升温超过1.5度，然后我们降低排放，大气层冷却下来会发生什么。

sentences.en: and that the repercussions of that failure, the pain inflicted on countries like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这是一种可能的情景。

sentences.en: and the rest of the world will then prompt the country, the United States, to adopt carbon pricing.
sentences.zh: 诺德豪斯也承认这确实是一个更有可能的情景。

sentences.en: Is that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 你是否担心这些事情不会及时发生？

sentences.en: That is a specific scenario that the scientists envision and lay down the report.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它们不会及时阻止1.5度的升温。

sentences.en: And so they looked at what happens if emissions go up, we heat up past that 1.5, and then we bring emissions down and the atmosphere cools back down.
sentences.zh: 他一点也不乐观，认为我们能避免那1.5度。

sentences.en: And they looked at that as the likely scenario.
sentences.zh: 他认为就目前的情况来看，我们无法避免2度的升温。

sentences.en: And Nordhaus acknowledged that that is a more likely scenario as well.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能在未来20年内迅速行动，我们可以阻止它。

sentences.en: And are you worried that these things won't happen in time?
sentences.zh: 但如果我们不这样做，我们将面临更大的变化，

sentences.en: Well, they're not going to happen in time for 1.5 degrees.
sentences.zh: 地球系统的变化，我们只能猜测，无法真正理解，因为它超出了过去20万或30万年的历史经验范围，

sentences.en: He is not at all optimistic that we will avoid that 1.5.
sentences.zh: 也许是100万年。

sentences.en: He doesn't think right now, based on the way things are going, that we will avoid 2 degrees.
sentences.zh: 科学家和经济学家都说，一个很可能的结果是，落实政策，你超调了，然后你再把情况扭转回来。

sentences.en: If we start moving swiftly in the next 20 years, we can stop it.
sentences.zh: 我们不能等10年，因为我们刚刚听说我们只有10年时间，所以我们不应该等9年。

sentences.en: But if we don't do that, we're off to much larger changes,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们等了11年才采取措施，那也比永远等待要好。

sentences.en: changes in the Earth system that we really can only guess at and can't really understand because it's outside the range of historical experience in the last 200,000 or 300,000 years,
sentences.zh: 科拉尔，如果我们超调了，如果我们突破了1.5度和2度的升温，有没有可能到那时我们已经失去了太多的基础设施，

sentences.en: maybe a million years.
sentences.zh: 失去了太多解决这个问题所需的人员和资源，以至于再也无法完成了？

sentences.en: Both the scientists and the economists say a real likely outcome is that get the policies in place, you overshoot, and then you bring things back down.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，世界上还会剩下足够多的人来以有效的方式实施这个计划吗？

sentences.en: We can't wait 10 years because we just heard we only have 10 years, so we shouldn't wait nine years.
sentences.zh: 嗯，全球变暖的影响分布非常不均。

sentences.en: But if we wait 11 years and then take steps, then that's better than waiting forever.
sentences.zh: 世界上受影响最严重的地区和人口是低洼的沿海国家，

sentences.en: Coral, if we overshoot, if we blow past 1.5 and 2 degree warming, is it possible that at that point we've lost so much infrastructure,
sentences.zh: 在1.5度或2度的升温情景下，孟加拉国沿海的大部分人口可能会变成国际难民。

sentences.en: so much of the personnel and the resources required to fix this, that it can't be done anymore?
sentences.zh: 非洲许多已经在与干旱作斗争但仍能种植作物的国家，将经历一个转变，即再也无法种植作物。

sentences.en: I mean, will there be enough of the world left to implement this in a way that could be effective?
sentences.zh: 我们会看到原本艰难的耕地变成沙漠。

sentences.en: Well, the impacts of global warming are very unequally distributed.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致粮食短缺，甚至饥荒。

sentences.en: The parts of the world and the populations that will experience the most severe impacts are low-lying coastal nations,
sentences.zh: 报告阐述了那种情景，以及与这些影响相关的许多政治动荡和破坏。

sentences.en: probably most of the population of coastal Bangladesh in a 1.5 or 2 degree warming scenario will be turned into, you know, international refugees.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我们将遭受巨大的经济打击。

sentences.en: A lot of countries in Africa that are already grappling with drought but can still grow crops will experience a transition to no longer ever being able to grow crops again.
sentences.zh: 当然，海岸线将受到海平面上升的严重冲击。

sentences.en: We'll see sort of cropland that's struggling turn into desert.
sentences.zh: 我们将继续经历越来越强的风暴。

sentences.en: And that will probably lead to food shortages and perhaps famine.
sentences.zh: 但总的来说，世界上最富有的部分将会适应。

sentences.en: The report, you know, lays out that scenario and a lot of political unrest and disruption associated with those impacts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果出现粮食短缺，还有转基因食品。

sentences.en: Here in the United States, we'll take a big economic hit.
sentences.zh: 像孟山都（Monsanto）这样的公司已经在寻找新的种植地点，在加拿大种植玉米，利用不同的生长季节。

sentences.en: Certainly, the coasts will be hit hard with rising sea levels.
sentences.zh: 所以在世界上最富有的地区，我们将看到技术和财富被部署来帮助我们适应。

sentences.en: We will continue to experience stronger and stronger storMs.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这仍然是一个相当严峻的情景。

sentences.en: But overall, the richest part of the world will adapt.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个情景中，我们看到了全球经济不平等的鸿沟在不断扩大。

sentences.en: You know, if there's food shortages, there's genetically modified foods.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果出现粮食短缺，就会有转基因食品。

sentences.en: Already, companies like Monsanto are looking at new places to grow crops, growing corn in Canada, using different growth seasons.
sentences.zh: 孟山都这样的公司已经在寻找新的农作物种植地，比如利用不同的生长季节在加拿大种植玉米。

sentences.en: So in the richest parts of the world, we will see technology and wealth being deployed to help us adapt.
sentences.zh: 因此，在世界上最富裕的地区，我们将看到科技和财富被投入使用，以帮助我们适应环境。

sentences.en: I mean, this is still a pretty grim scenario.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这仍然是一个相当严峻的局面。

sentences.en: And it is one in which we see such an increase in the divide of global economic inequality.
sentences.zh: 而且在这种局面下，我们看到了全球经济不平等鸿沟的进一步扩大。

sentences.en: The poor and the suffering will be made far more poor and suffering and numerous as a result of global warming.
sentences.zh: 全球变暖将导致贫困和受苦的人们变得更加贫困、更加痛苦，且人数更多。

sentences.en: And that's where we will likely then see governments say, OK, this is absolutely not a hoax.
sentences.zh: 届时我们很可能会看到各国政府表态：好吧，这绝对不是什么骗局。

sentences.en: This is a real thing.
sentences.zh: 这是真实存在的事情。

sentences.en: And we still have a little bit of time to save ourselves and maybe make the world not quite as bad as it is now.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一点时间来拯救自己，或许能让世界不至于变得像现在这么糟糕。

sentences.en: Let's go ahead and slap that price on carbon.
sentences.zh: 让我们行动起来，给碳排放定价吧。

sentences.en: Let's try to fix this.
sentences.zh: 让我们试着解决这个问题。

sentences.en: And how many years do we have before there's an overshoot threshold?
sentences.zh: 在达到超调阈值之前，我们还有多少年时间？

sentences.en: If the world were to act along the lines of the recommendations of this report and implement Nordhaus's plan, what's the time frame in which that has to be done?
sentences.zh: 如果世界各国按照这份报告的建议行事，并实施诺德豪斯的计划，那么必须在什么时间框架内完成？

sentences.en: If we were to avoid that overshoot scenario, we have two or three years.
sentences.zh: 如果我们想避免那种超调情景，我们只有两到三年时间。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: To get the policies in place, to get that carbon pricing implemented and to start the carbon pricing prograMs.
sentences.zh: 要落实这些政策，实施碳定价，并启动碳定价计划。

sentences.en: That's the prescription.
sentences.zh: 这就是药方。

sentences.en: And what is Nordhaus's goal in talking about all this, in sitting down with you and having this discussion?
sentences.zh: 那么诺德豪斯谈论这一切，与你坐下来进行这场讨论，他的目标是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think that he wants this idea to be at the center of the policy discussion for the 2020 campaign.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为他希望这个想法能成为2020年竞选期间政策讨论的核心。

sentences.en: I think that he would like to see this specific policy understood, embraced, and endorsed by the next president,
sentences.zh: 我认为他希望看到这项具体政策被下一任总统所理解、采纳和支持，

sentences.en: and thus to be something that is talked about and worked out as a policy proposal by the candidates who are running for president in 2020.
sentences.zh: 从而使它成为2020年总统候选人们在竞选时讨论并制定出的政策提案。

sentences.en: So he's basically saying presidential candidates should campaign on this, on a carbon pricing system, and that voters should vote on it.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是在说，总统候选人应该以此为竞选纲领，即建立碳定价体系，而选民应该就此进行投票。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Coral, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 科拉尔，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: It's always good to be with you.
sentences.zh: 和你在一起总是很愉快。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: After days of defending Saudi Arabia, President Trump reversed course on Thursday,
sentences.zh: 在为沙特阿拉伯辩护数日后，特朗普总统周四改变了立场，

sentences.en: expressing confidence in intelligence reports that suggest the kingdom played a high-level role in the assassination of Jamal Khashoggi,
sentences.zh: 表示相信情报报告，这些报告显示沙特王国在贾迈勒·卡舒吉的暗杀事件中扮演了高层角色，

sentences.en: a journalist who was highly critical of Saudi Arabia's leaders.
sentences.zh: 卡舒吉是一位对沙特领导人持强烈批评态度的记者。

sentences.en: What are you considering for possible consequences for Saudi?
sentences.zh: 你正在考虑对沙特采取什么可能的后果措施？

sentences.en: Responding to questions as he prepared to board Marine One, Trump said he was now weighing harsh punishments against Saudi Arabia.
sentences.zh: 在准备登上“海军陆战队一号”时回应提问，特朗普表示他现在正在权衡对沙特阿拉伯的严厉惩罚。

sentences.en: Well, it'll have to be very severe.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那必须是非常严厉的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's bad, bad stuff.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是非常、非常恶劣的事情。

sentences.en: But we'll see what happens.
sentences.zh: 但我们会看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: Intelligence reports indicate that Saudi agents close to the country's crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman, beat, tortured,
sentences.zh: 情报报告显示，沙特王储穆罕默德·本·萨勒曼身边的沙特特工殴打、折磨，

sentences.en: and dismembered Khashoggi the moment he walked into the Saudi consulate in Turkey.
sentences.zh: 并在卡舒吉走进位于土耳其的沙特领事馆的那一刻将其肢解。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严密控制的机器运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我和萨拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.zh: 请在任何你获取播客的地方收听。
